idea.title: Integrating Automated Novelty Checking into Chain-of-Ideas Scientific Generation Frameworks
idea.research_problem: How to dynamically filter and direct multi-step scientific idea generation paths using automated literature-grounded novelty assessment.
idea.research_gap: Current chain-based and iterative LLM ideation frameworks effectively capture progressive domain developments and simulate peer reviews, but they lack real-time integration with rigorous, facet-based novelty checking mechanisms, often resulting in incremental ideas that overlap with existing literature.
idea.methodology: We propose a modular pipeline combining Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) agent generation with an Idea Novelty Checker retrieval-augmented re-ranking module. During each step of the iterative idea evolution chain, candidate generation paths are queried against a vector database of scientific literature using a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank approach. If a candidate idea exhibits high semantic overlap and low facet-level divergence compared to existing papers, the novelty checker injects specific negative constraints and citation gaps into the prompt context, forcing the CoI agent to pivot towards unexplored directions before proceeding to subsequent refinement steps.
idea.expected_contribution: A unified framework that bridges automated literature-grounded novelty checking with multi-step research ideation agents, significantly improving the originality and technical depth of generated scientific proposals without requiring model training.
idea.experimental_setup: We select a benchmark set of 100 recent computer science and NLP problem statements from public conference repositories. We compare three configurations: standard CoI agent generation, a baseline with random literature retrieval augmentation, and our proposed novelty-guided CoI pipeline. Each method generates 3 distinct research proposals per problem statement.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate the generated proposals using a dual-pronged approach: (1) Automated novelty scoring using the Idea Novelty Checker framework to measure distance from historical literature embeddings, and (2) Expert-aligned LLM judging protocols (Idea Arena) evaluating feasibility, technical depth, and overall scientific impact.
feasibility_assumptions: API access to frontier language models is available for agentic generation and prompt execution.
Pre-computed academic vector embeddings and retrieval indices from baseline literature sets can be queried locally or via public APIs.
Experiments can be fully executed within a 6-week timeframe using Python orchestration scripts.

idea.title: Prompt-Guided Iterative Multi-Agent Refinement for Scientific Ideation with Feasibility Control
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent language model dialogues be optimized to generate scientific research ideas with high novelty while mitigating systematic medium-novelty biases and preserving technical feasibility under hardware-constrained environments?
idea.research_gap: Prior work explores multi-agent LLM dialogues and retrieval-based novelty checking independently or relies on computationally prohibitive hidden-state probes. Existing prompt-driven frameworks struggle with medium-novelty bias and lack an accessible, token-space intervention loop balancing novelty and feasibility on consumer hardware.
idea.methodology: We propose a unified token-space framework combining multi-agent dialogue loops with prompt-guided novelty and feasibility control, distinct from hidden-state extraction methods like ThinkProbe-Respond (2026.findings-emnlp.574). We instantiate a generator agent and a critic agent. During critique and revision steps, we use structured zero-shot scoring heuristics paired with retrieved literature snippets (via a retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker) to evaluate intermediate outputs. To prevent degenerate scoring and hallucinated metrics from an 8B base model, we constrain heuristics to rule-based textual facet overlaps. If the evaluated trajectory indicates medium-novelty bias, we intervene via explicit contrastive and structural prompts rather than latent-space probing. To isolate the true gain of this loop, we run an ablation comparing standard multi-agent critique loops against the proposed contrastive prompt-guided refinement.
idea.expected_contribution: This work delivers an automated, hardware-feasible scientific ideation system that integrates token-space novelty and feasibility checks into multi-agent loops, bypassing the medium-novelty bottleneck without requiring model weight training or hidden-state extraction.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize the RINoBench benchmark and an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework. Using an 8B quantized open-weights LLM running via bitsandbytes on a single 12 GB consumer GPU, we pre-compute and cache literature snippet embeddings to minimize active GPU memory overhead. We run multi-agent ideation sessions across computer science domains, comparing baseline multi-agent setups against our prompt-guided revision loop.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated ideas using RINoBench metrics, measuring rubric-based novelty scores, factual grounding against retrieved literature via a retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker, and human expert evaluation alignment for novelty and feasibility.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to local 8B open-source large language models quantized via bitsandbytes to fit within a single 12 GB consumer GPU.
Availability of public benchmark datasets like RINoBench and public scientific literature indices for retrieval.
Pre-computing and caching literature snippet embeddings effectively prevents active GPU memory overflow during multi-turn agent loops.

idea.title: Latent-Probed Multi-Agent Iterative Refinement for Novel Scientific Idea Generation
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent language model dialogues be optimized to generate scientific research ideas with high novelty while mitigating the systematic medium-novelty bias of language models?
idea.research_gap: Prior work explores multi-agent LLM dialogues for scientific ideation [2025.sigdial-1.26] and retrieval-based novelty checking independently [2025.sdp-1.9], and recent methods apply hidden-state probes strictly for novelty judgment tasks rather than generative steering [2026.findings-emnlp.574]. There lacks an integrated framework where latent-space probing of critic internal states is adapted to dynamically steer multi-agent generation loops away from medium-novelty biases during iterative refinement, without assuming unrealistic VRAM budgets or conflating judgment classification directly with causal token-level steering vectors.
idea.methodology: We propose a unified framework combining multi-agent dialogue loops with latent-space probing and rigorous prompt-based fallback mechanisms. We instantiate a generator agent and a critic agent using open-weights models (e.g., Llama-3-8B-Instruct) quantized to fit a single 12GB consumer GPU. To resolve the conflation between judgment representation and generative steering, we first evaluate a strong text-based contrastive prompting baseline powered by a retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker [2025.sdp-1.9]. Next, we adapt a lightweight linear probe trained on pre-extracted hidden states in an offline script to detect latent medium-novelty states. When a medium-novelty state is detected, rather than performing unstable activation patching on quantized weights, we trigger structured prompt modifications and structural contrastive interventions during the revision step.
idea.expected_contribution: This work provides a practical, automated scientific ideation system that integrates latent-space probing into multi-agent loops, achieving higher human-aligned novelty scores and bypassing the medium-novelty generation bottleneck within consumer-hardware resource constraints.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize the RINoBench benchmark [2026.lrec-1.370] and an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework running an 8B open-weights LLM via local 4-bit/8-bit quantization on a single 12GB consumer GPU. To bound inference latency and VRAM consumption while resolving hardware bottlenecks, we restrict the evaluation to single-turn critic probing configurations rather than unbounded multi-turn loops. We compare baseline multi-agent setups, text-based contrastive prompt ablations, random-trigger baselines, and our offline-probed prompt intervention loop across computer science domains.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated ideas using RINoBench metrics [2026.lrec-1.370], measuring rubric-based novelty scores, factual grounding against retrieved literature via a retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker [2025.sdp-1.9], and human expert evaluation alignment for novelty and feasibility.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to frozen open-source 8B parameter models running locally via standard Hugging Face libraries with 4-bit/8-bit quantization on a single 12GB consumer GPU.
Availability of public benchmark datasets like RINoBench [2026.lrec-1.370] and public scientific literature indices for retrieval.
Training a lightweight linear probe using a pre-extracted supervised dataset of annotated hidden states via an offline script within the 6-week project window.

To resolve memory and latency trade-offs under hardware constraints, we pre-compute and cache static background inspiration contexts to minimize real-time RAG overhead, and restrict activation extraction to target middle-to-upper layers rather than full residual streams. If a medium-novelty trajectory is flagged, we map the scalar activation score to structured contrastive prompts retrieved from cached inspirations, conditioning the downstream revision step to enhance technical depth and novelty.

idea.experimental_setup: We restrict local execution strictly to a quantized 8B open-weights model on a single 12GB VRAM consumer GPU. idea.title: Latent-Probed Multi-Agent Iterative Refinement for Novel Scientific Idea Generation
idea.research_problem: How can multi-agent language model dialogues be optimized to generate scientific research ideas with high novelty while mitigating the systematic bias of language models toward generating ideas of mediocre novelty?
idea.research_gap: Prior work explores multi-agent LLM dialogues for scientific ideation and retrieval-based novelty checking independently, but lacks an integrated framework where hidden-state novelty probing is used inside an ideation-critique-revision loop to dynamically steer agents away from medium-novelty biases during generation.
idea.methodology: We propose a unified framework combining multi-agent dialogue loops with latent-space novelty probing. Specifically, we instantiate a generator agent and a critic agent. During the critique and revision steps, we use a lightweight probe on the critic's hidden states to detect latent novelty assessments before final text generation. If the probed latent representation indicates a medium-novelty or unoriginal trajectory, we intervene by conditioning the subsequent revision step on explicit structural contrastive prompts derived from retrieved literature snippets, pushing the framework to produce higher technical depth.
idea.expected_contribution: This work provides a practical, automated scientific ideation system that integrates latent-space novelty probing into multi-agent loops, achieving higher human-aligned novelty scores and bypassing the medium-novelty generation bottleneck without requiring model weight training.
idea.experimental_setup: We utilize the RINoBench benchmark and an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework. Using a frozen 8B/70B open-weights LLM running via API/quantized local consumer GPU, we run multi-agent ideation sessions across computer science domains. We compare baseline multi-agent setups against our latent-probed revision loop.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate generated ideas using RINoBench metrics, measuring rubric-based novelty scores, factual grounding against retrieved literature via a retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker, and human expert evaluation alignment for novelty and feasibility.
feasibility_assumptions: Access to frozen open-source large language models via API or local quantization on a single consumer GPU.
Availability of public benchmark datasets like RINoBench and public scientific literature indices for retrieval.
